title: Airbyte Cloud security incident, Nov 2026
disclaimer: Made for entertainment using AI. Not endorsed by Airbyte, Salesforce, any government agency, news outlet, company, or anyone else named.
size_basis: Airbyte Cloud moves data between many companies' apps and databases, and every customer lost service for days. Airbyte says fewer than 1% of customers were directly affected. Salesforce also cut access. The full count is unknown.
who_is_affected: Companies that use Airbyte Cloud to sync data. API connectors for Salesforce, HubSpot, Intercom, Zendesk and others were still down as of 12:47 PM ET Nov 23. Affected customers were contacted by Airbyte; others need only watch its status page.

known.text: Airbyte says a security incident gave an attacker access to its systems; it blocked them and took Cloud offline on Nov 17.
Airbyte Cloud was offline for days; the service began coming back on Nov 19.
Airbyte says fewer than 1% of its customers were affected and that it contacted them.
As of 12:47 PM ET Nov 23, 16 API connectors (Intercom again among them), Connector Builder and MCP were still down as a cautionary measure.
Salesforce disabled the Airbyte connected app on Nov 20 and says this was not a Salesforce platform problem.

not_known.text: Whether customer data, credentials or metadata were accessed or taken.
How the attacker got in. Airbyte says a full incident report is coming.
Who is behind it, and what 'broader, global cyberattack' Airbyte means.
Whether Salesforce or other platforms' customer data was reached through Airbyte.

Whether self-managed Airbyte installs were affected.
